body:
**Clause.** IEEE 802.1AS-2011 11.2.15.3, Figure 11-8 (as corrected by Cor1). In WAITING_FOR_PDELAY_RESP_FOLLOW_UP, a second Pdelay_Resp with the same sequenceId takes the machine to RESET. That counts as a lost response, so repeated duplicate responses clear asCapable through the lost-response rule.

**Observed** at `55680bff`: from one point on, every Pdelay_Req is answered by two identical Pdelay_Resp and one Pdelay_Resp_Follow_Up. The end station keeps announcing every second for 16 s with no gap; asCapable is never cleared.

**Source.** `hdl/ucode/gen_gptp_ucode.py:1140-1176` (`_pdresp_arm_the_pairing`): the second response re-arms the pairing, documented at `:1170-1176` as "not a reset".

**Expected.** A duplicate Pdelay_Resp with the same sequenceId resets the exchange and counts as a lost response.

**Acceptance.** A test where 5 consecutive exchanges each carry a duplicate Pdelay_Resp: asCapable is cleared at the 5th (see the lost-response issue). A single duplicate does not clear it. A plant that restores the re-arm is caught.
title: A duplicate Pdelay_Resp with the same sequenceId re-arms the exchange instead of resetting it (802.1AS-2011 Figure 11-8)
